short: The Norman duke whose conquest rebuilt English landholding, church and language.
full:
William was crowned in Westminster Abbey on Christmas Day 1066, ten weeks after Hastings. Securing the country took far longer. Risings in the west, the fens and the north were suppressed piecemeal, the last with the Harrying of the North in 1069-70, a deliberate devastation of Yorkshire whose effects were still visible in tax records a generation later.

He held England by castle and by tenure. Motte-and-bailey fortifications went up in every shire, and by 1086 almost no major English landholder remained: the land was held from the king by roughly 200 Norman tenants-in-chief. Norman bishops replaced English ones and the church was reorganised on continental lines. In 1085-86 he commissioned the Domesday survey, an audit of who held what and what it was worth that has no European parallel. He died at Rouen in September 1087 of injuries taken while campaigning in the Vexin.
